title: The Impossible Summer
premise: Marine biologist Orsen Hartwell has spent ten years at a remote sea-turtle sanctuary training himself out of feeling, logging data instead of grief after the accident that took his brother. When a research consortium's anonymous pen-pal program pairs him with his bitter rival, conservation lawyer Wren Calloway, their letters crackle with old grievances until they become the only honest place either of them exists. Forced to co-lead a last-ditch nesting-season rescue threatened by a corrupt developer who owns both their futures, they discover the letters were never anonymous to him — Orsen has known all along, and Wren must decide whether love built on that deception can survive. In the end, as the hatchlings make their impossible run to the sea, Orsen finally says the sentence he has rehearsed for a decade — 'I should have saved him' — and chooses belonging over the safe, containable heart.
about_author: Juniper Dravenmoor is the pen name of a former field researcher who traded tide charts for typewriters and now writes love stories set where the land runs out. She lives on a windswept coast with an unreasonable number of houseplants and a dog named Buoy.

chapters.title: The Muscle That Lies
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV opens on the sanctuary's nesting beach, where he counts turtles and recites his creed: the heart is trainable, containable. The consortium's pen-pal assignment arrives, pairing him with 'Anonymous B' — whose first letter drips with familiar contempt for his methods. He realizes it's Wren Calloway, the lawyer who once tried to shut down his funding. Emotional beat: armored loneliness meeting an unexpected spark of anger that feels dangerously alive.

chapters.title: Letters in the Undertow
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Orsen and Wren as their letters shift from barbed professional rivalry to confessions neither would say aloud — her exile from a firm that sold out conservation, his brother's drowning. Meanwhile the developer Halvorsen arrives with permits to bulldoze the nesting dunes, forcing them onto the same island committee. Emotional beat: intimacy deepening in writing while hostility hardens in person, each unaware the other feels the same pull.

chapters.title: The Sentence Rehearsed
chapters.summary: Wren's POV at the climax: during a storm-night hatchling rescue, she discovers Orsen's draft letters — a decade of unsent pages addressed to her, proving he always knew her name behind 'Anonymous B.' Feeling surveilled and betrayed just as Halvorsen's corruption scandal breaks, she confronts him publicly, and Orsen finally speaks the rehearsed sentence: 'I should have saved him.' Emotional beat: betrayal and raw confession colliding as the rescue teeters on failure.

chapters.title: What the Tide Returns
chapters.summary: Dual POV resolution: Wren files the whistleblower case that sinks Halvorsen, then returns to the beach at dawn for the hatchlings' run. Orsen, no longer counting turtles instead of heartbreaks, admits the heart was never a muscle to contain but a tide to answer. She takes his hand; the letters become a book they write together. Emotional beat: quiet, earned belonging — survival's price paid, and love chosen anyway.
